notes: Production changes match the reference exactly: placeholder names are extracted from the checked CEL AST at provision time, and response retries are limited to expressions that read status, header or latency placeholders, or whose placeholder name is only known at evaluation time. The added tests cover every case the maintainers listed (request-only, upstream.host, escaped literal, status_codes near-miss, direct ph() calls, dynamic names) at both the matcher and handler level.

The non-test changes match the reference fix: placeholder names are pulled from the checked CEL AST, and only expressions that read response placeholders, or whose placeholder name is dynamic, are evaluated after the round trip. The tests cover the shorthand and `ph()` forms, escaped string literals, look-alike prefixes, upstream-selection placeholders and dynamic names, and check both hit count and response body.

The non-test changes match the reference: the `ParseableDiffPrefixes` builder is applied everywhere, the prefix strip is now single-component, `rename to`/`copy to` are used as a fallback, and the `diff --git` line is split where both halves name the same path. Existing command-arg test expectations were updated correctly, but the visible diff (truncated) shows no new parser tests for mnemonic, quoted or ambiguous paths.

The non-test changes match the reference: a ParseableDiffPrefixes builder is applied to every diff command, prefix stripping works on any single path component, rename/copy-to lines are used as a fallback, and the diff --git line is split symmetrically. The existing command-arg tests were updated to the new -c flags; the truncated diff hides whether parser-level tests were added.

The code change matches the reference exactly. It closes and unlinks under the mutex, adds an idempotent-close guard returning net.ErrClosed, closes the dup'd file to stop the fd leak, and skips abstract sockets. The added tests cover every review requirement for both unix and unixgram: unlink on last close, refcount survival, double close, racing close and relisten, and the abstract-socket sentinel.

The production change matches the reference: the fd leak in reuse is closed, Close uses a CAS guard plus the mutex for ref-counted unlink, and abstract sockets are handled; the added tests cover every review requirement for both unix and unixgram (abstract-socket test is Linux-only and writes a sentinel file into the package directory, cleaned up afterward).

Fixes the root cause: a reusable caller with children now re-aggregates its status from them instead of being forced straight to cancelled, and a run with no job updates is emitted so its concurrency group gets checked. It is slightly less precise than the reference, because it returns the caller as updated even when unchanged and emits whenever no jobs updated, not only when the run status changed. The two new tests are strong: one covers the cancelling cascade after the runner acknowledges, the other covers a force-cancel waking the blocked waiter.

C1 fixes both root causes and passes the hidden tests, but by a different route than the reference: `cancelOneJob` sends reusable callers with children to `RefreshReusableCallerStatus`, so the caller stays cancelling while any child is still cancelling, and `cancelRun` now emits the run when no job changed so blocked runs in the concurrency group can start. Weaknesses: it always returns the caller as updated, even when its status did not change; it relies on in-place mutation of the caller instead of re-reading the row; it emits on every no-op cancel rather than only when the run's status changed; and the no-children cancel branch partly duplicates existing code. Its model test (caller stays cancelling, then the runner acknowledgement cascades cancelled up) and its service test (force-cancel wakes the waiting run) are thorough.

Core symlink translation works in both backends: skip with a notice naming the flag, the .rclonelink suffix, target-length size, and ranged reads of the target. However, the zip side appends the suffix after root handling, so a root pointing at `link.rclonelink` behaves differently than in the squashfs side, and the zip side also restructures readZip to silently drop members under a symlink even without --links, plus pokes `dt[""]` directly, a likely cause of the failed hidden test and well beyond the reference's minimal change. Tests are thorough.

Symlinks are exposed as .rclonelink objects in both zip and squashfs, and List and NewObject agree on names, but the patch fails one of the two hidden tests and adds risky extras. The extras are zip members under a symlink being hidden even without --links, a forced root dir entry, and a squashfs single-file root change (f.file = o.Remote()) that can mis-name nested file roots. In zip, rooting directly at link.rclonelink does not resolve because root matching runs before the suffix is added. The tests are thorough.

The wrapper change matches the reference: Close/Reconnect reset the engine state and Get/Walk reconnect first, and the extra key/ContextEngineID resets are defensible. However, Gather now closes only once at the end, so later tables in the same gather still use the stale session instead of reconnecting on the next request, and it reports Close errors the reference ignores. The patch also rewrites the unrelated TestSnmpInitGosmi path for its own environment, and the full package suite fails.

Adds Close to the interface, makes Get/Walk reconnect, resets USM engine state (and context engine ID) only when reconnecting a closed connection, and closes after a failed gather including the StopOnError path. Departures from the reference: the close is deferred to the end of the agent's gather rather than happening right after the first failure, the reset is duplicated in Close, and TestSnmpInitGosmi was edited for unrelated reasons; the package suite failure is unexplained and may be environmental.

The design matches the reference: it tracks the latest exemplar timestamp per series, keeps the series through gc and gcSeries while the exemplar is at or after minValidTime, and releases chunks, appender and mmap-ready state; but it changes the signatures of the internal stripeSeries.gc and gcSeries, which likely breaks existing test call sites (e.g. s.gc(0, 0)), consistent with the 0/3 hidden tests and the failing package suite, and the truncated diff leaves the append, WAL replay and snapshot hooks unverified despite extensive new tests.

The visible GC logic follows the reference closely: it keeps series that have an exemplar at or after the cutoff, releases their chunks and appender, decrements the mmap-ready count, and leaves actualMint unaffected. However, it changes the internal `stripeSeries.gc`/`gcSeries` signatures, and the tsdb package suite fails with 0/3 hidden tests passing, which most likely means existing callers no longer compile, so the extensive new tests may never have run.
